prompt: The best way to provide enough homes in large cities is to build tall apartment blocks. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay:
As the population of large cities continues to grow, providing sufficient housing has become a major challenge for governments. I strongly agree that constructing high-rise apartment buildings is the most effective solution because it makes efficient use of limited land while promoting sustainable urban development.

One of the primary advantages of tall apartment blocks is that they maximise land use. Unlike detached houses, which occupy large areas of land, high-rise buildings can accommodate hundreds of families within the same space. As a result, cities can meet the growing demand for housing without expanding into surrounding green areas. This helps reduce urban sprawl, preserve natural habitats and minimise deforestation, all of which contribute to environmental sustainability and help mitigate the effects of climate change.

Another important benefit is that apartment living better reflects the lifestyle of many modern families. Smaller households generally require less living space and spend less time maintaining large properties. In addition, apartment complexes are often built close to schools, hospitals, shopping centres and public transport networks. This allows residents to commute more easily, reduces travelling time and improves their overall quality of life. Cities such as New York and Toronto demonstrate how well-planned high-rise developments can provide comfortable housing while supporting efficient urban infrastructure.

In conclusion, I believe that high-rise apartment buildings are the most practical way to address housing shortages in large cities. They not only provide accommodation for a growing urban population but also encourage sustainable development, protect the environment and improve the quality of life for city residents.
